title: No bachelors, no biryani, no dogs: What your RWA can legally ban, and what it can’t
content: Resident welfare associations possess limited powers governed by law and their own documents.  RWAs can manage common areas and enforce valid bye-laws for community well-being.  However, associations cannot override individual legal or proprietary rights of residents.  Rules must have a proper basis and be applied fairly to all members.  Disputes often arise from unclear rules and the need for greater transparency.

title: Amit Shah hails South's development in CMs meet, cites 3 pillars of progress
content: Chairing the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Tamil Nadu's Mahabalipuram, the Union home minister said: "The people of South India and the governments have also established many excellent traditions in the fields of innovation and revenue generation." He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

title: Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in 2027 assembly election
content: Uttar Pradesh elections now prioritize women voters, who are a significant electoral force.  Women's turnout has consistently surpassed men's in recent  polls.  Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers.  Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters.  Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
content: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk and Meta software engineer, founded Contenda after a hackathon.  She and three friends turned a pandemic-era project into a successful startup.  The company focuses on helping businesses repurpose technical content effectively.  Contenda secured one million dollars in pre-seed funding in March 2021.  Chen now leads the company as its chief executive officer.

title: 'We are Gen Z' row: Army veteran's crowdfund offer for woman to serve in Siachen
content: A retired Army officer criticized a tourist's viral rant at a Kargil checkpoint. He stated her behavior unfairly portrayed the younger generation and created division. The officer offered to crowdfund her salary to serve in challenging locations. He defended security personnel and emphasized Kashmiris' equal partnership in India. The incident occurred during VIP movement which caused temporary traffic restrictions.

title: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected 23rd president of Bangladesh
content: Alamgir secured 255 votes in Thursday's presidential election held at the Jatiya Sangsad, Bangladesh's Parliament. His rival, Oli Ahmed, the candidate backed by an 11-party opposition alliance led by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party (NCP), received 88 votes. The voting took place between 2 pm and 5 pm local time under the supervision of chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.

title: Meet 10-yr-old Hsu Ting-wei, winner of Silicon Valley invention award
content: At the Silicon Valley International Festival, Taiwanese innovators caught the global spotlight with remarkable inventions. A ten-year-old prodigy took home a prestigious award for crafting an AI-driven electronic nose capable of detecting hazardous substances and potentially stopping disease outbreaks. This year, Taiwanese competitors celebrated a landmark achievement, claiming twenty-four gold medals and numerous honors, showcasing their ingenuity and practical solutions that captivated both judges and audiences.

title: NASA launches $500,000 challenge to improve space weather predictions
content: In an effort to enhance the understanding of upper atmospheric conditions, NASA is inviting proposals for affordable technology solutions. The Orbital Clarity Challenge aims to refine predictions regarding satellite orbit variations caused by atmospheric drag. Participants stand to win up to $500,000 for their innovative concepts, along with the opportunity for a free test flight to test their technologies.

title: Steam tug that survived two world wars reappears in Serbia after drought
content: Amidst severe drought, a historic steam tug once lost beneath the Sava River has resurfaced, delighting locals who flock to witness 'Sava's Titanic'. This vessel, which sank in 1945 after a tragic encounter with a mine, revitalizes memories of the Balkans' complex history. Its emergence underscores the grim water shortages plaguing significant European rivers today.

title: Anthropic's AI designed proteins in 2 days, a job that takes scientists months
content: Anthropic says Claude designed protein binders that worked against 14 of 15 targets, with Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience validating 354 binders from 1,320 designs. Hit rates reached 35.1%, well above the field's usual 10-15%. A separate test saw Claude Opus 5 match a contract lab's purity reading in 19 minutes. Protein design stays blocked in Fable 5 over bioweapon risks.

title: Chandigarh was built as a planned city. So why does it keep sinking in the rain?
content: Chandigarh's planned infrastructure faces recurring monsoon flooding issues. Intense rainfall exposed vulnerabilities in various city sectors and major roads. Vehicles were stranded and markets submerged after a short, heavy downpour. The city's drainage system appears inadequate for current rainfall intensity and urbanization. This recurring problem highlights the need for infrastructure upgrades beyond emergency responses.

title: Gangster shot dead outside Haryana court; 14 rounds fired, 1 attacker caught
content: Gangster Vinod Panu alias Kana was shot dead in the Hisar court parking area. Two other individuals sustained injuries during the shooting incident which involved many rounds. Police apprehended one suspect at the scene and recovered a weapon from him. The deceased gangster faced numerous criminal cases, including murder charges. Investigations are ongoing to determine the full scope of the incident and potential accomplices.

title: John Cena vs CM Punk net worth comparison: Who is richer in 2026?
content: John Cena holds a substantial net worth advantage over CM Punk in 2026.  Cena's extensive WWE career and major Hollywood roles built his fortune.  CM Punk also earned millions from wrestling, UFC, and AEW ventures.  However, Punk's ventures outside WWE did not match Cena's financial scale.  Cena's broader entertainment career provided him a clear financial lead.

title: 'He ain’t making it': Cristiano Ronaldo Jr sparks concern over football future
content: Cristiano Ronaldo's oldest son has sparked major outrage as many feel he is not that interested in making a career in football.

title: Morgan Rielly addresses trade rumours, Maple Leafs' future ahead of 2026 season
content: This season, Morgan Rielly is optimistic about remaining with the Toronto Maple Leafs. As training camp approaches, trade speculations have quieted down. Rielly expresses appreciation for being part of the team’s future and is dedicated to improving after a tough previous season. His focus remains on playing at his best to drive team success.

title: Gill’s eye for talent: How a Mohali youngster’s life changed after one net session
content: A Rs 20,000 Sher-e-Punjab T20 contract could prove to be a life-changing opportunity for Kirandeep Singh, a youngster from village Cholta Kalan in Mohali. But his journey to Fazilka Falcons began earlier, when Shubman Gill spotted his bowling and urged him to leave tennis-ball cricket behind.

title: ‘Don’t go chasing the IPL’: Pujara’s plea for Manav Suthar after Galle heroics
content: Cheteshwar Pujara has encouraged young spinner Manav Suthar to prioritize his development in Test cricket, emphasizing the importance of maintaining his natural bowling style for the longer format instead of adapting to white-ball games. Having performed admirably in his first two Tests, Pujara sees the flighted deliveries of Suthar as essential for success. Recently, India celebrated a notable World Test Championship triumph.

title: Kochi postgraduates bag Rs 10 lakh grant for startup making inland mud-crab farming easier
content: Innovators from Kochi have crafted a groundbreaking technology for mud-crab farming, effectively tackling issues such as cannibalism and the requirement for brackish water. Their novel system enables farming in inland regions, broadening geographical opportunities. With a generous ₹10 lakh grant awarded for their remarkable achievement, this technology opens up premium crab farming to a wider community of farmers.

title: 'She cheated on me': SBI banker kills wife, sister; posts chilling WhatsApp status
content: A State Bank of India employee allegedly shot his estranged wife outside her workplace. He then reportedly returned home and shot his younger sister. The employee then turned the gun on himself, ending the tragic sequence. A WhatsApp status accusing his wife of cheating was found. Police are investigating the marital dispute and the events.

title: Spain break 23-year-old cricket record held by Ponting and Waugh's Australia
content: Spain are currently playing in the Men's T20 World Cup Sub Regional Europe Qualifiers in Southern Finland and have won all their matches in the tournament so far. Their latest victory came against Bulgaria on August 18, when they chased down a target of 60 in just 29 deliveries, winning by nine wickets.

title: Watch: ‘Modi Chalisa’ at Press Club of India sparks row; act draws clarification
content: In response to a viral video, the Press Club of India confirmed that the event featuring an aarti for a Prime Minister Narendra Modi statue was not sanctioned by them. The hall had been rented for a press conference by an external organization, but the terms of the rental were breached. The club took immediate action to stop the event, issuing a clarification via social media about their involvement.

title: Homes struggle, factories thrive: How AI is reshaping the US economy
content: US housing starts fell sharply in July, reaching their lowest point since November 2022.  Existing home purchase contracts also declined, hitting their weakest level since January.  High borrowing costs and limited inventory continue to impact housing affordability and sales.  Meanwhile, US factory output reached its highest level in over four years.  This manufacturing growth was driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence and related industries.

title: England pacers cut Pakistan Test match ball in half; here's why
content: Robinson took 5 for 51 and Tongue claimed 5 for 46 as Pakistan were bowled out for 171 on the first day of England's first Test under Joe Root's second stint as full-time captain following Ben Stokes' retirement from international cricket.

title: No home to return to: Assam’s flood victims face harder fight after waters recede
content: Assam's floodwaters have receded, but families face immense challenges rebuilding their lives.  Destruction of homes and essential supplies marks the beginning of a new struggle.  The government is assessing damage and providing initial financial assistance to affected households.  Restoring livelihoods and infrastructure remains a significant hurdle for many residents.  The long-term recovery process continues as the state addresses ongoing flood and erosion issues.

title: ‘Why is she wearing shorts’: How family outing at Pune fort turned into assault
content: Police registered a case against eight members after an assault.  The incident occurred at Sinhagad Fort following an argument over a girl's attire.  The group allegedly questioned and then physically assaulted the complainant and his family.  Similar complaints were also received from other visitors to the historical fort.  Authorities have launched a search to apprehend the eight accused individuals.

title: 'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul attacks Sangh over ideology
content: Speaking at the "Hara Bhara Swaraj: A Tribute to Rajiv Gandhi's Vision" programme, the Gandhi Scion described the ideological contest in India as a deeper struggle over how people understand themselves, freedom and their place in society. The Congress leader also drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj', saying no organisation or individual could claim to know what is true for another person.

title: NSE shares may trade on its platform under 'permitted-to-trade' route: Report
content: The National Stock Exchange is considering a groundbreaking move to trade its own shares directly on its platform, potentially skipping the need for additional approval from Sebi. By leveraging its existing 'permitted-to-trade' mechanism, the NSE could facilitate trading of shares already listed on other recognized exchanges, making NSE shares available for its own trading after an initial listing elsewhere.

title: India, Japan deepen defence ties with maritime security pact as China challenge looms
content: India and Japan's defense ministers met to expand their strategic partnership. They signed an agreement enhancing maritime security cooperation between their navies. This pact facilitates information sharing and disaster relief efforts. Both nations are also exploring joint shipbuilding and reciprocal ship repair facilities. Future plans include joint exercises and a defense industry forum.

title: Poonam Pandey defends Govinda amid wife Sunita Ahuja's affair allegations
content: In a surprising turn of events, Poonam Pandey has stepped up to defend Govinda amid his wife Sunita Ahuja's allegations. Pandey firmly supported Govinda, rejecting claims of his involvement with another woman. Meanwhile, Sunita was spotted at a family court with their son Yashvardhan, igniting divorce rumors. However, Govinda's manager later reassured fans that Sunita has decided to withdraw her earlier divorce petition.

title: 'We hope for the players' support': BWF on India Open in Delhi pollution
content: BWF secretary general Thomas Lund defends the India Open's February scheduling despite Delhi's pollution concerns, urges players to support the calendar and outlines the sport's plans for a 15-point scoring system, greater technology use and synthetic shuttlecocks.

title: BWF Worlds: Treesa-Gayatri stun 7th seeds to reach quarters, medal one win away
content: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a World Championships quarterfinal spot.  The unseeded Indian pair defeated Japan's seventh seeds in straight games.  Treesa's aggressive play and Gayatri's structural support proved decisive.  This victory marks a significant step in their comeback after Treesa's injury.  A medal is now guaranteed with one more win at the event.

title: 'My best shot': Nasa astronaut shares image of 2025 Maha Kumbh taken from space
content: Astronaut Donald Pettit has unveiled breathtaking photographs of the 2025 Maha Kumbh Mela, captured from the International Space Station. These stunning images showcase the vibrant Hindu pilgrimage, shimmering against the vast darkness of space. The event, held in Prayagraj, attracted millions for ritual bathing, marking it as one of the largest gatherings in human history. This expedition also contributed to ongoing scientific research efforts.

title: No 2800 km dash this time: Qamran Iqbal arrives early, ready for Duleep Trophy challenge
content: Called up less than 24 hours before the Ranji Trophy final, Qamran Iqbal travelled nearly 2,800 km from Srinagar to Hubballi before scoring an unbeaten 160 that helped Jammu and Kashmir win their maiden title. The 24-year-old reflects on the whirlwind journey, J&K's rise and his ambition to shine in the Duleep Trophy. North Zone will take on West Zone at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) from Sunday.

title: Kurnool Ridge School to host CBSE South Zone Archery Championship from August 23
content: The championship is expected to witness participation from over 650 schools and more than 2,000 young archers from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry

title: Six industrial parks to be developed in A.P. under Central scheme: Minister
content: The six proposals have been submitted through the prescribed BHAVYA process and are currently under consideration by the Government of India under the challenge route, Commerce Minister T.G. Bharath tells the A.P. Assembly

title: Attempt to set ablaze auditorium at Tumari in Shivamogga, leaves theatre-lovers, writers shocked
content: The 40-year-old auditorium has been the venue for hundreds of theatre and cultural events over the decades. It has been a cultural centre in the island of Tumari, surrounded by backwaters of Sharavathi

title: Andhra Pradesh Assembly adopts Central amendment Act on water pollution
content: It replaces rigid criminal penalties for minor administrative and technical violations with structured financial penalties

title: Hotel leaseholder arrested, two detained after Kolkata hotel inferno kills nine
content: Of the nine, seven are Bangladeshi nationals and one each from Bihar and West Bengal; the hotel’s owner, Bireshwar Mitra, is still absconding, said police

title: U.S. Ambassador Gor arrives in Ladakh on maiden visit, undertakes river rafting
content: The trip marks Mr. Gor's first tour of Ladakh since assuming office as U.S. Ambassador to India, providing an opportunity to experience the region beyond official engagements

title: Prohibition of construction near NH: Keralam to approach Supreme Court
content: Apex court has prohibited the construction of residential buildings within 40 metres  and commercial establishments within 75 metres from the midpoint on either side of national highway

title: GBA’s Freedom from Waste campaign: Will it be enough to keep Bengaluru’s 1,616 blackspots from reappearing?
content: Each blackspot represents the larger interaction between collection efficiency, waste processing capacity, enforcement, and institutional coordination. Thus, clearing these blackspots may remove the symptom, only for it to reappear within a short time.

title: Andhra Pradesh has fertilizer stock enough to meet projected requirement till October, says Agriculture Minister Atchannaidu
content: The app-based distribution system has streamlined supplies and so far 5.69 lakh farmers have received fertilizers through the new system, he tells the Legislative Assembly

title: Won't let Bihar become 'police State': Tejashwi Yadav
content: Tejashwi Yadav said Bihar's law and order had "completely collapsed", while accusing the government of failing to control "rising police brutality"

title: Drug trafficking: two accused teachers released in police custody
content: The teachers were recently arrested and remanded in judicial custody for allegedly functioning as financial intermediaries for inter-State drug traffickers. Their role was uncovered following the arrest of Safwan, the first accused in the case from Vadakara.

title: Conductor suspended for letting student issue tickets on KKRTC bus
content: He left the electronic ticketing machine unattended which was used by the student to issue 11 tickets to passengers on the bus

title: APCRDA allots returnable plots to 23 farmers from Undavalli
content: The plots comprising 26 residential and 15 commercial plots allotted through an online e-lottery system

title: CPI(M) opposes direct mayor election, but backs quota for BCs
content: Direct election to the posts of mayor and chairperson will lead to concentration of power, it says and cautions the government against rushing through the reservation process to meet deadlines linked to Finance Commission grants

title: Assam transporters blockade Meghalaya vehicles after violence at Shillong students’ rally
content: Masked men on bikes with covered registration plates went on rampage during a Khasi Students’ Union rally, targeting Meghalaya government and Assam-registered vehicles and assaulting bystanders

title: Karnataka SIR: Over 43.80 lakh voters to get notice; over 20 lakh flagged for ‘logical discrepancy’
content: Notices will be served to 23.45 lakh people who could not find their own or their parents’ details in the 2002 electoral roll.

title: 36 Hours in Srinagar: A first-timer’s guide to Kashmir’s capital
content: Explore Srinagar in 36 hours with this itinerary covering Dal Lake at sunrise, the heritage lanes of the downtown area, Jamia Masjid, Khanqah-e-Moula, Lal Chowk, Asia’s largest tulip garden, and an authentic wazwan feast

title: Routine disagreements not mental cruelty: HC; rejects man's divorce plea
content: The court also said that cruelty in a marriage cannot be determined by a few isolated instances and the entire married life should be assessed as a whole

title: Amit Shah says Congress’s decision on rendering first two stanzas of Vande Mataram is ‘anti-national’
content: Home Minister says Congress’s decision to render only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram reflects “appeasement politics” and alleges that the 1937 resolution laid the foundation for Partition

title: Sajjan Kumar: From Congress veteran to convict
content: Sajjan Kumar had been in custody since December 2018, when he surrendered following the Delhi High Court’s decision to overturn his acquittal in a case relating to the killing of five members of a Sikh family and the burning of a gurdwara.

title: Mayiladuthurai fisherman injured in alleged shooting dies in Saudi Arabia
content: He is the second fisherman to have lost his life after a fisherman Maveeran was killed recently; the two were part of a group of four fishermen engaged in fishing in Saudia Arabia when they were allegedly shot

title: All arrangements in place for 72nd Nehru Trophy Boat Race in Keralam
content: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the event at 2 p.m. on August 22, following the morning heats for smaller boats starting at 11 a.m. Seventy-one boats, including 22 snake boats, are vying for victory.

title: UKG student dies after teacher tries to strip, slaps him in Visakhapatnam classroom
content: CCTV footage appears to show the teacher stripping him in front of the class to shame him, then slapping him. He collapsed moments later

title: Jagan dares government to CBI probe on DSC; Lokesh says he can’t tell APPSC from DSC
content: The YSRCP president said the SIT set up by the present government had found no irregularities in the Group-I recruitment, and that his party had written to the Prime Minister and the Union Home Minister seeking a CBI inquiry into the 2025 DSC

content: At South Zonal Council Meeting, V.D. Satheesan also urges Union government to annul the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026,

title: Cockroaches in kitchen, ‘unsafe’ food storage: FDA suspends food licences of more Mumbai eateries
content: FDA action follows a statewide crackdown on August 18, during which 31 hotels, restaurants and dhabas were inspected. Five food licences were suspended, and improvement notices were issued to 22 establishments

title: ‘Khalifa’ movie review: Prithviraj Sukumaran stars in a shoddily written old-school smuggling drama
content: Director Vysakh’s ‘Khalifa’, starring Prithviraj Sukumaran, suffers from an outdated story and a flat narrative, with even a cameo from a superstar failing to make up for its shortcomings

title: CPI(M) holds Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary responsible for circular on student participation in Left parties’ protests
content: Mr. Shanmugam contended the meeting (where the decision to curb protests was taken), attended by the Chief Secretary, had denied students their right to protest.

title: No motive behind circular on student participation in CJP, Left parties’ protests: Tamil Nadu Higher Education Minister
content: The Minister’s statement comes after a now-withdrawn directive issued by the Higher Education Department, which had sought coordinated action to prevent students from participating in protests organised by the Left parties and CJP

title: Death sentence for preacher found guilty of sexually assaulting four minor girls in Tirunelveli
content: S. Abraham, 50, who had been running a prayer hall at Mela Ilanthaikulam, sexually assaulted the minors under the guise of taking moral science classes for them in 2022

title: D.K. Shivakumar seeks ‘fairness’ for Southern states in devolution and delimitation
content: Pride demands fairness in return. We have always done our part. We contribute, we build, we grow, and we carry the nation forward. All we ask from the Union government is this: please care as much as we share: Karnataka Chief Minister

title: Gadchiroli mining project: Bombay HC asks petitioner to approach National Tiger Conservation Authority
content: The court was hearing the matter on the 937-hectare mining project in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli district and its potential impact on tiger movement corridors and wildlife habitat

content: The aim is to transform cooperatives in Tamil Nadu into people-centric, transparent and economically sustainable institutions, with the objective of ensuring their sustainable growth and stability and enhancing their market competitiveness

title: Tamil Nadu Assembly: State government to launch health insurance for the elderly
content: Another key announcement is the planned replacement of the 87-year-old Tamil Nadu Public Health Act, 1939, with a modern, comprehensive Act to address contemporary and future health challenges

title: ‘New health cover is one step in Tamil Nadu’s geriatric outreach’
content: The steady rise in India’s ageing population requires a healthcare system that is differently oriented to address their evolving needs, officials say

title: Popular film shooting spots to be developed in Tamil Nadu: Tourism Minister
content: The project aims to provide facilities such as experience centres, signages, parking spots, and refreshment areas

title: Prakash Raj says ‘end of fascists is closing,’ hails youth activism
content: Addressing DYFI meet, actor says young protesters have ‘punctured the Centre’s ego’ and that ‘we are not afraid of you’

title: On Camera, 6-Year-Old Falls Face First, Dies After Being Slapped By Teacher
content: The family has alleged that the incident was not an isolated act of physical punishment, claiming that other children had also been beaten. They have demanded strict action if the allegations are established.

title: "Papa Smiling, Looking Down Proudly At His Beautiful Sonia": Rahul Gandhi
content: Rahul Gandhi shared his mother Sonia Gandhi's upcoming memoir, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love", expressing pride that her life's journey would finally be shared with the public.

title: "May God Protect Her": YouTuber As Man Kills Sister, Mentions Her In Post
content: Pragya Mishra's sister Divya was murdered by the latter's husband Manas, who then killed his own sister and himself as well

title: Bhutan Nominates Former Election Body Chief For SAARC Secretary General Post
content: According to reports, Dasho Sonam Topgay's name has been proposed by Bhutan, as under the alphabetical order that SAARC follows, it is Bhutan's turn to nominate the next Secretary-General of the regional body.

title: "Slim" Chances Of Bangladesh PM Visiting India Without Mutual Trust: Top Aide
content: The domestic mood in Bangladesh, with the escalation of anti-Hasina sentiments, remains a major issue in Bangladesh politics and relations with India, and Rahman's government does not want to risk being seen as being soft on Hasina.

title: Opinion: Opinion | An India-Pakistan War Test: How Far Would Saudi Arabia And Turkey Go?
content: India must shed its hesitation to get into deeper alliance arrangements with regional partners. Many Gulf states had approached India in the past for treaty arrangements, but India has been somewhat chary.

title: Supreme Court Sets Up Panel To Probe Cop Action, Violence During NEET Protests
content: The top court has directed that allegations of harassment and molestation - particularly those involving female protesters - be treated as a priority. Additionally, an inquiry will be conducted into the serious and severe injuries sustained by protesters during police action.

title: Jharkhand Government's Order Cancelling JPSC, JSSC Exams Stayed By High Court
content: The Jharkhand government decided to cancel the 22 recruitment examinations based on findings of CID and SIT investigations into alleged irregularities in various competitive examinations.

content: The court, announcing its verdict, also imposed fines totalling Rs 2.70 crore on the six convicts on Thursday, according to a statement issued by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

content: Speaking to NDTV for the first time since the video went viral, the woman said she regretted her remarks and had never intended to insult the armed forces or become popular through the incident.

content: The Supreme Court also emphasised that the suicide notes, while reflecting the dead person's anguish, could not by themselves establish the requisite mens rea on the part of the accused.

content: The student was found dead at his home in Khandala, located in the Vaijapur taluka of Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district.

content: Police suspect that the racket was dealing not only in counterfeit medicines but also in anti-cancer drugs allegedly diverted from hospitals and government institutions.

content: If you hold a Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) account, you still get four free withdrawals every month. Nothing changes there.

title: How an 18-year-old turned $10 abandoned storage units into a $135,000 business
content: he buys storage units across the tri-state area without knowing exactly what is inside, then sorts through the contents looking for objects that can be resold . the idea grew from a habit he picked up as a child, when he sold books on eBay and held onto discontinued Lego sets . by high school, he was also thinking about college and how he might distinguish himself from applicants with stronger academic records .

title: Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, convicted in 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, dies at 80
content: former congress MP was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 anti-sikh riots in Delhi . he was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi high court on December 17, 2018 in a case involving the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara .

title: China puts 'robocops' on traffic duty; a 'Superman' robot claims it can outrun Bolt
content: the 1.88-metre, 98-kg robot, developed by SUPCON Information, is being deployed to handle routine traffic-control duties . it uses cameras, radar and onboard computing to identify helmetless e-bike riders, passengers on ebikes, vehicles crossing stop lines and pedestrians violating signals . the robot has no power to arrest and does not carry a gun .

title: Centre gives nod to set up a bench of J&K HC in Ladakh
content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday decided to set up a bench of high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh. In a post on X, Union home minister Amit Shah said the government is "fully committed" to the all-round development of Ladakh and claimed that the decision will enhance access to justice to citizens living in remote areas. "The Union cabinet, under the leadership of the PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, has decided to set up a bench of the high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh," Shah said. "This will significantly enhance access to justice for citizens living in remote areas of Ladakh by reducing the time required to avail themselves of the legal services they are entitled to. The Govt is fully committed to the all-round development of Ladakh and to ensuring constitutional safeguards," he added.

End of Article

title: NEET protests: SC sets up 5-member panel to probe excessive use of force by cops
content: the top court said a five-member panel will be headed by former SC judge justice R Subhash Reddy . the committee will examine allegations of excessive use of force against students during the student march over the NEET paper leak . it will also look into police surveillance, the proportionality of crowd-control measures, and the provision of medical assistance and compensation to victims .

title: Secret Hormuz corridor: How US kept ships, oil moving despite Iran threat
content: the operation allowed 15–20 tankers to move through a southern channel of the strait each night under US military guidance . this carried close to 10 million barrels of oil a day, half the volume that passed through the waterway before the war . the previously unreported operation has provided a crucial channel for keeping oil exports moving at a time when the conflict has severely disrupted one of the world's most important energy routes .
